messages.author: da5542c86290b629
messages.subject: Programming with `summarise`
parts:
I have a data set containing information about customers, the various stages they reached in the purchasing process and whether or not they were contacted in-between these stages. I'm looking to analyse whether or not contacting a customer increases the conversion rate to the next stage in the process. 

I'm trying to create a function using dplyr that will allow me to specify the column describing whether contact occurred and the column describing whether the customer reached a given stage. The result should be the conversion rates for contacted/not contacted. Here is where I'm up to:

library(dplyr)

sample.size <- 50

lsample <- function() {
  sample(c(TRUE, FALSE), sample.size, replace = TRUE)
}

# Table of customers, whether they were contacted prior to each phase in the purchase process
# and whether they completed those phases
df <- data.frame(Id = 1:sample.size, 
                 Contacted.before.submit = lsample(),
                 Submitted = lsample(),
                 Contacted.before.purchase = lsample(),
                 Purchased = lsample())

# Conversion to submit
to.submit <- df %>% group_by(Contacted.before.submit) %>%
  summarise(Count = n(), Converted = sum(Submitted), Rate = Converted / Count)

# Conversion to purchase
to.purchase <- df %>% group_by(Contacted.before.purchase) %>%
  summarise(Count = n(), Converted = sum(Purchased), Rate = Converted / Count)

# Try it with a function...
rollup <- function(data, contact.ind, conversion.ind) {
  data %>% group_by_(contact.ind) %>% 
    summarise_(Count = n(), Converted = sum(conversion.ind), Rate = Converted / Count)
}

# This causes 'Error in n() : This function should not be called directly'
rollup(df, ~Contacted.before.submit, ~Submitted)

The `rollup` function fails complaining that `n()` should not be called directly. I've seen mention of this error in conjunction `plyr` clashes. I don't _think_ this is my problem. The output of `conflicts()` is:

"df"        "filter"    "lag"       "body<-"    "intersect" "kronecker" "setdiff"   "setequal"  "union"

messages.author: b756a7daa2c2aa6d
messages.subject: Re: Programming with `summarise`
parts:
If you're going to use summarise_() you need to quote all the inputs:

contact_ind <- ~Contacted.before.submit
conversion_ind <- ~Submitted
sum_f <- lazyeval::interp(~sum(var), var = conversion_ind[[2]])

df %>%
group_by_(contact_ind) %>%
summarise_(Count = ~n(), Converted = sum_f, Rate = ~Converted / Count)

The formulation with interp is a bit inelegant - I definitely need to
think about this more.

Hadley
